$comment: Every key pxsig.config.json and pxsig.workspace.json allow (packages/pxsig/schema), for `pxsig help <key>`. test/help.test.mjs fails when a schema key has no entry here.

version.operation: Read to know the file format; nothing else changes.

name.meaning: Project name in a single-package repository: this key, else the package.json name without its scope, else `default`. In a monorepo the workspace key is the name.
name.operation: The name --project takes, and the name in reports and the dashboard.

srcRoot.meaning: The folder whose stories belong to this project. A story's component is its folder relative to srcRoot.
srcRoot.operation: Which stories become entries, how they group into components, and which edits can change them.

storybook.meaning: Where Storybook is and how its paths resolve.

storybook.url.meaning: Where Storybook serves index.json and iframe.html: a dev server or a static build.
storybook.url.operation: Every render, manifest build and story-index read goes here.

storybook.configDir.meaning: Storybook's config folder, used to resolve index.json's story paths when Storybook lives outside the project.
storybook.configDir.operation: How story files are matched to entries.

storybook.staticDir.meaning: A built Storybook (index.json + iframe.html). When nothing answers at storybook.url, check, manifest and the server serve this folder themselves on a free 127.0.0.1 port.
storybook.staticDir.operation: Checks keep working without a running Storybook.

store.meaning: Where baselines and run output live.

store.dir.operation: Where baselines, the approval log, reports and renders are written.

store.layout.meaning: Where baselines go: in the store, or beside each component.
store.layout.operation: package: <store>/baselines/<component>/<id>.psig. colocated: <srcRoot>/<component>/__pxsig__/<id>.psig, so a component and its baselines move together in reviews.

capture.meaning: How each story is rendered and captured.

capture.viewport.meaning: Browser viewport, [width, height] in CSS pixels, at device scale 1.
capture.viewport.operation: The size every render is taken at, unless a mode or story sets its own.

capture.settleMs.meaning: Minimum wait after fonts load, before the layout-stability wait.

capture.target.meaning: The element captured. A story can override it.
capture.target.operation: What part of the page each baseline shows.

capture.waitFor.meaning: Extra waits for content that animates in script: { selector, minMs?, stableMarkup? }, each applied when its selector matches.
capture.waitFor.operation: Fewer flaky entries for stories with animation.

grid.operation: Finer grids catch smaller changes and cost more. Changing it changes every new baseline.

minCellPx.meaning: Adaptive grid: cells at least this many pixels wide, capped by grid. 0 turns it off.
minCellPx.operation: Small components get fewer, larger cells, so noise does not trip the gate.

detail.meaning: Write the detail channel (full-resolution tiles where edges are) into new baselines.
detail.operation: Catches thin changes (borders, icons) the grid averages away.

trim.meaning: Crop renders to their content (right and bottom) before checking: { pad, tolerance }, or false.
trim.operation: A story that grows or shrinks its empty space does not fail.

gate.meaning: The gate for every entry: an entry fails when any rule trips. A story can set its own.
gate.operation: How big a change must be to fail a run. See gate.threshold and the keys beside it.

gate.threshold.meaning: Per-cell mean RGB delta (0–255) that counts a cell as changed.
gate.threshold.operation: Lower catches subtler colour changes and fails more often.

gate.minCells.meaning: Fail when at least this many cells changed. 0 turns the rule off.

gate.minSsim.meaning: Fail when SSIM is below this.
gate.minSsim.operation: Higher fails on smaller structural changes.

gate.maxChangedPct.meaning: Fail when more than this percentage of cells changed.

gate.maxEdgePct.meaning: Fail when the edge-map difference is above this percentage.
gate.maxEdgePct.operation: Catches outline and layout shifts that keep colours similar.

gate.detail.meaning: The detail-channel rule: { blockDelta, energyDelta, minTiles }, or false.
gate.detail.operation: How thin changes in the detail tiles fail an entry.

modes.meaning: Named render settings: { globals, colorScheme, viewport, browser, extends }.
modes.operation: Each mode is one more entry per story: a theme, a density, a browser.

defaultMode.meaning: The mode whose entries keep the bare story id.
defaultMode.operation: Which entries have ids without an @mode suffix.

modesByDefault.meaning: Modes every story is rendered in, unless the story says otherwise.
modesByDefault.operation: How many entries each story makes.

suites.meaning: Extra manifests (manifest.<suite>.json) for other mode sets.
suites.operation: A larger set checked separately, for example nightly.

affects.workspaceDeps.meaning: A change in the source of a workspace package this project depends on selects every entry.
affects.workspaceDeps.operation: Safer selection in a monorepo, at the cost of full checks when a dependency changes.

affects.extra.meaning: More paths whose change selects every entry (the Storybook config folder, a lockfile).

affects.ignore.meaning: Globs for changed paths that select nothing when nothing traced claims them (docs, other apps, CI config). $workspace/ and $repo/ anchor a glob; otherwise it is relative to the project.
affects.ignore.operation: Without it, a change outside srcRoot makes `check --since` check every entry. Never hides a baseline, a store file or an imported module.

nonVisual.meaning: Top-level folders under srcRoot with no visual stories; their stories are reported as excluded.
nonVisual.operation: Those stories are never rendered or checked.

a11y.operation: Accessibility violations are recorded per entry and compared with a11y.json.

integrity.meaning: Integrity options for doctor and the ledger.

integrity.requireBaselineImages.meaning: Report missing-baseline-image when a baseline has no image.
integrity.requireBaselineImages.operation: Whether a baseline without an image is an error.

integrity.staleAfterSourceChange.meaning: Report stale when a source changed after a verdict.
integrity.staleAfterSourceChange.operation: Whether `stale` and doctor flag out-of-date verdicts.

integrity.sourceRoots.meaning: Folders, relative to the workspace root, whose edits can make a verdict stale.

integrity.maxTracedFiles.meaning: Above this many edited files, staleness falls back to "same component folder" instead of the import graph.
integrity.maxTracedFiles.operation: Large edits are judged faster and less precisely.

integrity.indexTimeoutMs.operation: How long doctor waits before scanning the files instead.

integrity.renderSkewMs.meaning: A render written this long after its verdict makes the verdict stale.
integrity.renderSkewMs.operation: How a re-render without a re-check is noticed.

integrity.manifests.meaning: Other manifests, relative to the store, whose baselines are not orphans.
integrity.manifests.operation: Which baselines doctor counts as in use.

importPathPattern.meaning: Advanced: a regular expression selecting the story files, with the component folder as group 1.
importPathPattern.operation: Which story files belong to the project, when the folder rule does not fit.

dashboard.meaning: The dashboard rebuilt on this project's design system.

approvals.meaning: How approvals are recorded and guarded.

approvals.identity.meaning: What each approval and repair log line says about who made it: none (the default; the commit that adds the line and the pull request say who), or git-email (the git email, as before 0.4.0).
approvals.identity.operation: With none, pxsig writes no personal data into the store; with git-email every new log line carries a by field.

approvals.level.meaning: How approvals are guarded: standard (a typed phrase at a terminal, or the dashboard with the dashboard link). strict is reserved for a later release and refused for now.
approvals.level.operation: Only standard exists today; any other value stops every command with a setup error.

dashboard.ui.meaning: A UI adapter for `pxsig dashboard build` and `gaps`: a path to its module, relative to this folder, or a built-in adapter's name.
dashboard.ui.operation: pxsig serve serves this project's build while it is current.

projects.meaning: Project name to project folder, relative to the workspace root. Each folder holds a pxsig.config.json.
projects.operation: Which packages pxsig checks, and their names.

defaults.meaning: Any project config key, applied under each project's own config. "$workspace/" paths resolve from the workspace root.

requires.meaning: The pxsig versions this workspace needs, as a range: >=0.4.0, or >=0.4.0 <0.6.0, with || between alternatives.
requires.operation: A pxsig outside the range refuses to run here (exit 2, naming the range), and doctor warns about installs outside it. pxsig 0.3.x does not read the key.

server.port.meaning: Port pxsig serve tries first; if it is taken, the next ten are tried.
